t: The ancestors of Aboriginal Australians reached Sahul, the land that joined Australia and New Guinea, 50,000 to 65,000 years ago, and may have settled across the continent within 6,000 years of landing.
More than 400 distinct peoples, each with its own language and Country, pass down their beliefs through dance, stories, songlines and art, which together tell of creation in the Dreaming.

From 1788 British colonisation brought disease, frontier war and dispossession: in the 150 years that followed, 90% of Indigenous Australians died, and between 1910 and 1970 between 10 and 33 percent of Aboriginal children were removed from their families.
dyk: A 2011 study of DNA from an early-20th-century lock of an Aboriginal person’s hair found that, outside Africa, Aboriginal peoples have lived continuously in the same territory longer than any other human population.
ev: British colonisation begins at Port Jackson with the arrival of Governor Arthur Phillip and the First Fleet
Pemulwuy begins a guerrilla war against the settlers around Sydney, carried on by his son Tedbury until 1810
About 200 people leave Cummeragunja Station in protest at their treatment, in the Cummeragunja walk-off
The Wave Hill Walk-Off begins, a strike over working conditions that grows into a claim to the land
A referendum passed by a 90% majority gives Aboriginal affairs to the federal government and removes discriminatory census provisions from the Constitution
The Aboriginal Land Rights Act lets Aboriginal people in the Northern Territory claim land by traditional association
In the Mabo Case the High Court declares terra nullius invalid and recognises native title
Prime Minister Kevin Rudd makes a formal apology for the Stolen Generations

f.homeland: The Australian mainland, Tasmania and many islands, excluding the Torres Strait Islands; as many as 500 linguistic and territorial groups, among them the Yolngu of Arnhem Land, the Arrernte and Warlpiri of central Australia, the Pitjantjatjara, the Noongar, the Koori and the Palawa; today about a third in New South Wales and a quarter in Queensland.
f.period: arrival 50,000–65,000 years ago and settlement of the whole continent within about 6,000 years; Tasmania cut off by rising seas; the dingo and new languages and tools about 4,000 years ago; British colonisation from 1788 and frontier conflict to about 1930; protection laws and the removal of children, from 1869 to 1970; the 1967 referendum; land rights from 1976 and native title from 1992.
f.known: Country and the Dreaming; songlines, dance and stories; rock art and the dot painting of Papunya Tula; more than 250 languages at European contact, and sign languages; networks of trade across the continent; ancestral spirits such as the Rainbow Serpent, Baiame and Bunjil; some of the oldest continuous cultures on earth
f.sources: Aboriginal oral histories, such as those the Yolngu have passed down through hundreds of generations; rock art dated by modern techniques; archaeology and the 2021 migration models; genetic studies; the journals of the First Fleet and colonial records; historians of the frontier such as Broome and Reynolds and the University of Newcastle massacre project; census counts and language surveys.
